bug_info.bug_desc: The AES control FSM used one CLEAR state for both clearing input-side registers (initial key, IV, data-in, previous data-in) and waiting for the cipher-core clear handshake. Because CLEAR remained the current state until cipher_out_valid_i was accepted, data_in_we_o drove the data-in register clearing for more than one cycle. The data_in_new_d status tracker was reset using data_in_we_o, so when the FSM finally returned to IDLE and data_in_we_o deasserted, the write-enable activity associated with the clear (all four data_in_qe_i bits high) could be ORed into data_in_new_q. This made a cleared/partially-written input block appear complete, so automatic mode could start before all four data input registers had been written, violating the input-ready and automatic-start specifications.
bug_info.fix_hint: Split the clear operation into two FSM states: CLEAR_I, which clears the initial key, IV, data-in and previous-data input registers for exactly one cycle, and CLEAR_CO, which performs the cipher-core clear handshake and clears output data/trigger bits. Rename and re-encode the states accordingly. In the data-in status tracker, clear data_in_new_d using the all-four data_in_qe_i pulse (&data_in_qe_i) instead of data_in_we_o, so the clear write-enable pulse resets the tracker instead of arming it after returning to IDLE.
